answer: Under cohort-melt re-verification, each epoch the raven ledger secretly maps every identity into one of √N random cohorts, and each cohort must jointly finish a VDF whose difficulty grows with member count before cedar-signed results are accepted. An attacker packing 100 fakes into shared cohorts pays VDF cost scaling quadratically, roughly 10,000 units versus 100 for honest agents, a 100-fold penalty. A yarrow farmer running one genuine identity waits only one normal cohort delay per epoch, so honest agents pay linear, minimal cost while mass attackers face an infeasible nonlinear burden.
